title: Evaluation of the Safety and Efficacy of Rimonabant on Cognitive impairment in patients with post-COVID-19 Syndrome.
official: Effects of a CB1 Receptor Antagonist/Inverse Agonist (Rimonabant) on the Improvement of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Post-COVID-19 Syndrome (RIMOCOVID-1)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of rimonabant in improving cognitive impairment in patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome compared to placebo.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Be aged between 18 and 75 years (both inclusive).
2. Have had COVID-19 at least 3 months before joining the study.
3. Have been diagnosed with active PCS (Long COVID).
4. Have ongoing problems with memory or concentration due to long-COVID syndrome.
5. Show signs of cognitive impairment in study assessments.
6. Be willing to complete study assessments.
7. Be able to understand and speak Spanish.
8. Provide written consent to participate.
9. Indication of brain fog symptoms: BFS (Brain Fog Scale) ≥ 47
Exclusion criteria:
1. Have an active or recent COVID-19 infection.
2. Have other medical conditions that could explain their symptoms.
3. Have severe lung, heart, liver, kidney, or bone disease
4. Have a body mass index (BMI) greater than 40 kg/m²
5. Are unable to walk or attend study visits.
6. Use substances or medications that may affect memory or concentration.
7. Major depressive disorder or severe anxiety disorder, according to DSM-5-TR criteria: Scores ≥ 20 on the BDI-II or ≥ 11 on the HADS at screening, followed by the confirmation of the diagnosis by a health professional (psychologist or psychiatrist).
8. Are taking medicines that may interact with the study treatment.
9. Have a known allergy to rimonabant.
10. Have taken part in another clinical trial within the last month.
11. Are pregnant or breastfeeding.
12. Are able to become pregnant or father a child and are not using effective contraception.
13. Have a high risk of suicide.
14. Have severe mental health conditions (as per clinical records): major depressive disorder; severe anxiety disorder; bipolar disorder; schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder; psychotic disorder; previous suicide attempt; any psychiatric disorder requiring psychiatric hospitalization; any other severe psychiatric condition that, in the investigator's opinion, may compromise participant safety or interfere with study
15. Have neurological conditions that may affect memory or concentration.
